scope: Bounded read-only verification of public professional information. Promotion requires confirmed identity, Saudi-market basis, buying authority, plausible custom-software need, and at least one primary source. Unknown technical capacity is neutral.

scoring_contract.active_rule: No D-band record may be active. A/B records require two independent sources, including at least one primary or official source.

promoted.name: Abdulrahman Almuqati CIPD
promoted.product_stage: pre-company; patent-pending concept seeking a technical co-founder
promoted.technical_capacity: The founder explicitly states that he is solo and is seeking a technical co-founder; no broader internal technical-team conclusion was made.

confirmed_identity.reason: The exact personal profile and founder-authored venture job listing identify the same person and current founder role.

saudi_market_basis.reason: The profile is based in Riyadh, and the venture listing says the founder is working toward Saudi incorporation and cites a Saudi patent application.

buying_authority.reason: The listing identifies Abdulrahman as the solo founder choosing a founding technical partner.

plausible_custom_software_need.reason: The product requires computer vision plus on-device, mobile, and cloud software integrated with wearable hardware.

has_primary_source.reason: The founder-authored role and venture-owned company page are first-party sources.

product_intent.reason: A same-day role requests a technical co-founder for a specifically described AI wearable and its mobile/cloud delivery stack.

outsourcing_likelihood.reason: The solo founder explicitly seeks an external technical co-founder to build the product.

budget_readiness.reason: The offer is described as equity-based rather than salaried; no cash build budget, paid pilot, procurement, funding, or revenue is disclosed.

timing.reason: The technical-partner request was published on the verification date.

source_independence.note: The evidence is published in distinct LinkedIn objects controlled by the individual profile and venture. It is not cross-validated by an external news or program source.

evidence.paraphrased_evidence: The listing names Abdulrahman Almuqati as Vision Mate's solo founder, describes a wearable AI vision-assistance device with computer-vision and on-device/mobile/cloud components, says a Saudi patent application is under substantive examination and Saudi incorporation is in progress, and seeks an equity-based technical co-founder.
The exact-name profile places Abdulrahman in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia and identifies him as a current founder and operating executive.
The venture page describes Vision Mate as a wearable AI vision-assistance product and lists a company size of one, consistent with the pre-company solo-founder stage.

promoted.name: Hayath Kargal
promoted.product_stage: pre-MVP; Saudi entity formation and pilot planning

confirmed_identity.reason: The exact personal profile and founder-authored post identify Hayath Kargal and BookMyGuide consistently.

saudi_market_basis.reason: The current profile places the role in Jeddah, while the product post describes a Saudi-first marketplace, Saudi pilots, and Saudi entity formation.

buying_authority.reason: Hayath identifies himself as a co-founder applying the venture to an MVP program and planning its Saudi pilots.

plausible_custom_software_need.reason: The planned product is a Saudi-first booking marketplace, which plausibly requires custom web or mobile marketplace software.

has_primary_source.reason: The product-stage evidence comes directly from the co-founder.

product_intent.reason: The co-founder describes a specific marketplace, pre-MVP program application, Saudi entity work, and planned city pilots within the last year.

outsourcing_likelihood.reason: Technical capacity and external-builder intent are unknown; silence is not treated as evidence for or against outsourcing.

budget_readiness.reason: An MVP-program application is reported, but acceptance, funding, revenue, paid pilots, procurement, and a build budget are not verified.

timing.reason: LinkedIn displayed the qualifying post as approximately seven months old, within 365 days but outside 180 days.

source_independence.note: The record is C-band, so the A/B two-source rule does not apply. Both items are first-party and should not be represented as independent external corroboration.

evidence.source_title: Hayath Kargal - BookMyGuide MVP Lab application post
evidence.paraphrased_evidence: Hayath describes BookMyGuide as a Saudi-first marketplace, names himself and a co-founder, says the venture is pre-MVP and applying to NTDP MVPLab, and reports work toward a Saudi entity and pilots in Saudi cities. LinkedIn displayed the post as roughly seven months old; no exact publication date was exposed.
The exact-name profile presents Hayath's BookMyGuide role in a Jeddah context and is consistent with the founder-authored product post.

gaps.detail: Only 2 records passed every active-lead gate without weakening evidence standards; 10 examined records remain unresolved.
Several attractive technical-co-founder posts are first-person LinkedIn evidence only. A/B promotion requires a distinct program, venture, product, or official source.
Company/job pages for Bagi and Operon SA describe credible Saudi software needs but do not expose a named person with buying authority.
Multiple cohort discoveries date to 2024. They require a current founder-controlled or official update before promotion.

limitations: Research used only publicly visible professional pages and search-result excerpts in read-only mode.
No follows, connections, reactions, comments, saves, publications, messages, form submissions, extensions, or automated profile traversal were used.
No private personal identifiers were collected; canonical professional-profile URLs are retained only for identity and deduplication.
LinkedIn relative-age labels were not converted to invented exact dates; published_at remains null where the exact date was not exposed.
The accepted count is intentionally below ten because the remaining records lacked a required gate, source independence, freshness, or named authority.
